en: A ramp does not reduce total work to lift an object; it only reduces the effort force needed by spreading that work over a longer distance.
Friction between your shoes and the ground is what pushes you forward when you walk, not just what slows you down.
A bowling ball and a feather dropped inside a vacuum chamber hit the ground at exactly the same time because gravity accelerates all objects equally.
A magnet's north pole attracts another magnet's south pole, but two north poles pushed together will repel each other instead of attracting.
Electrons in a wire drift very slowly, but the electrical energy transfers nearly at the speed of light through the complete circuit.
The Moon does not produce its own light; it only reflects sunlight toward Earth, which is why we can see it glow at night.
Sound travels faster through water than through air because water molecules are packed more closely together to pass vibrations along.
A metal spoon feels colder than a wooden spoon at the same room temperature because metal conducts heat away from your hand faster.
A ball held at the top of a hill has stored gravitational potential energy even while still, which converts to kinetic energy as it rolls down.
A lever does not create extra force; it trades distance for force, so pushing down a longer distance on one end lifts a heavy load a shorter distance.
A magnet can attract a paperclip through a sheet of paper because magnetic fields pass through non-magnetic materials like paper and plastic.
A straw looks bent in a glass of water because light changes speed and bends when it passes from water into air, a process called refraction.
